newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US remain far apart on insurance - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US remain far apart on insurance - MOF.

text.p: Japanese and U.S. negotiators remain far apart on how to open Japan's $382 billion insurance market despite an on-going effort to find a solution over key issues, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.

"We are at the final stage (with the approach of December 15 deadline), so both sides are trying to carry on the negotiations constructively. However, we still remain far apart," the ministry official told reporters at a late-night briefing.

The first day of the planned two days of talks between Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, and senior U.S. Trade Representative negotiator Ira Shapiro were still going on, he added.
"We are clarifying our positions but at the same time we are trying to push the negotiations forward by searching for points to agree on despite our big differences," he said.
The two sides are also trying to set up a ministerial-level meeting ahead of the agreed December 15 deadline, which the official said will definitely be met.

Japan has also explained to the United States its five-year plan to deregulate insurance premium rates and to allow banks, securities houses and insurance companies to enter each others' business areas under Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's "Big Bang" financial reform scheme, the official said.
Japan and the United States are at odds over the implementation of a 1994 bilateral agreement to open Japan's insurance market.

Washington has accused Tokyo of reneging on the agreement by moving to deregulate its "third sector" niche insurance market -- the personal accident and health care insurance sectors -- in which foreign firms have a strong foothold, before opening its much larger primary life and casualty markets.

The dispute has become a major trade irritant between the two countries. They had originally set a July 31 deadline to settle the dispute, but agreed in October to push back the deadline to December 15.
